meta.title: Battery chemistry comparison for the Theseus slide: Li-ion vs Li-polymer vs alkaline AA (+ NiMH eneloop, + lithium AA)

labels.DS: datasheet/official spec (Battery University reference-handbook ranges are filed under DS and flagged in notes)

chart_suggestions: Bar: Wh/kg by chemistry with two bars for alkaline (25 mW vs 1 W) to show the collapse
XY: E91 energy (mWh) vs drain (mW) with the mouse load band 6.6-29.6 mW shaded as the sweet spot
Bar: share of the 29 g budget eaten by each cell (LiPo 26%, L91 52%, AA 79%, eneloop 93%)
Scatter: Jauch LiPo family capacity vs mass, with Theseus battery-mass budget line

takeaways: Per gram at mouse-level drain (~25 mW), a fresh alkaline AA (163 Wh/kg) is NOT worse than a small LiPo pack (123-153 Wh/kg). The case against AA is the 23 g single lump (79% of a 29 g mouse), single use, and collapse under load (40 Wh/kg at 1 W), not raw energy per gram. Say this honestly on the slide; it is a stronger argument than "LiPo is denser".
Li-ion cylindrical cells reach 243 Wh/kg (NCR18650B) but nothing that size fits a 29 g mouse; mouse-sized pouches lose energy density to packaging and the protection board.
Charge speed is set by the cell datasheet: the Jauch 250 mAh pack allows 0.5C max (125 mA), eneloop NiMH 1C (~57 min to -dV), alkaline 0.
Longevity: 500 cycles x 32-146 h per charge = 16,000-73,000 h of use for the Jauch pack [DV]; an alkaline AA is ~127 h at the 8 kHz load.
